certificate: the note: every even N >= 4 is p + eta with Omega(eta) <= 4, under GRH (arithmetic check)
status: This certificate checks arithmetic given the cited theorems; it does not prove the cited theorems. The tail regime (N >= 1e170) depends on the hypothesis scope of the explicit linear sieve theorem ([BJS] Theorem 6), which is under repair (see the repository README).

regime1.cited: Oliveira e Silva, Herzog, Pardi, Math. Comp. 83 (2014), as quoted in [BJS] section 1 and [JS] section 1

citations.source: Oliveira e Silva, Herzog, Pardi, Math. Comp. 83 (2014), as quoted in [BJS] section 1 and [JS] section 1
citations.statement: Every even N with 4 <= N <= 4e18 is a sum of two primes.

citations.source: Johnston, Starichkova, arXiv:2208.01229v3 (numbering of the v3 PDF)
citations.statement: Let x >= X2 >= 4e18 and 3 <= q <= sqrt(x), (a,q) = 1. Assuming GRH, |pi(x;q,a) - li(x)/phi(q)| <= c_pi(X2) sqrt(x) log x with c_pi(X2) = 3/(8 pi) + (6 + 1/pi)/(4 log X2) + 6/log^2 X2 + li(2)/(sqrt(X2) log X2).
citations.hypotheses: X2 >= 4e18 (validated here); x >= X2 and 3 <= q <= sqrt(x), (q, a) = 1 (validated by the caller as named checks)

citations.source: Bordignon, Starichkova, arXiv:2211.08844v1, quoting Schoenfeld, Math. Comp. 30 (1976), Corollary 1
citations.statement: If RH holds, |pi(x) - li(x)| <= sqrt(x) log x/(8 pi).
citations.hypotheses: x >= 2657.  [BS] prints 'for 3 <= x', which is false at x = 3; the range x >= 2657 is the one usually attributed to Schoenfeld and is the one validated here. Every use in the certificate has x >= 30000.

citations.statement: omega(N) < 1.3841 log N/log log N for N >= 3.
For x >= 1e9: sum_{n<=x} mu^2(n) <= 0.608 x and sum_{n<=x} mu^2(n)/phi(n) <= log x + 1.333 + 58/sqrt(x) <= 1.1 log x.
citations.hypotheses: x >= 1e9 (checked as log x > log 1e9 in intervals)

citations.source: Johnston, Starichkova, arXiv:2208.01229v3 (numbering of the v3 PDF)
citations.statement: For all N >= 71, |A| > N/log N, where A = {N - p : p <= N, p does not divide N}.

citations.source: Johnston, Starichkova, arXiv:2208.01229v3 (numbering of the v3 PDF)
citations.statement: (3.1) sum_{p<x} 1/p >= log log x + M0 - 2.964e-6/log x, x >= 2; (3.2) sum_{p<x} 1/p <= log log x + M0 + 1.614e-3, x > exp(8.9); (3.3) sum_{p<x} 1/p <= log log x + M0 + 6.836e-6/log x, x > 1e12.
For 2 <= x <= 1e12: log log x + M < sum_{p<=x} 1/p < log log x + M + 2/(sqrt(x) log x).

citations.reference: Theorem 6 'The linear-sieve, explicit version' (TeX label theo:JR) and Table 1
citations.statement: If 0 < eps <= 1/74 and prod_{p in P\Q, u <= p < z} (1 - g_n(p))^{-1} < (1+eps) log z/log u for all n and 1 < u < z, then for D >= z: S(A,P,z) < (F(s) + eps C1(eps) e^2 h(s)) X_A + R, and for D >= z^2: S(A,P,z) > (f(s) - eps C2(eps) e^2 h(s)) X_A - R, s = log D/log z, R = sum_{d | P(z), d < QD} |r(d)|; h(s) = e^-2 (1<=s<=2), e^-s (2<=s<=3), 3 s^-1 e^-s (s>=3).
citations.hypotheses: 0 < eps <= 1/74 (validated: the row used has eps' = 1/k with k >= 74 and eps < eps'); D >= z^2 for the lower bound and D >= z for the upper bound (validated by the caller as s >= 2, s_min >= 1).  The product hypothesis is proved in note section 4.2 under the fixed-z reading; the proof of the theorem uses it at all levels below z as well.

citations.source: Bordignon, Johnston, Starichkova, arXiv:2207.09452v6 (= Cai, Lemma 2); monotonicity of f, F from Johnston, Starichkova, arXiv:2208.01229v3 (numbering of the v3 PDF) section 2
citations.statement: F(s) = 2e^gamma/s for 0 < s <= 3; F(s) = (2e^gamma/s)(1 + int_2^{s-1} log(t-1)/t dt) for 3 <= s <= 4; f(s) = 0 for 0 < s <= 2; f(s) = 2e^gamma log(s-1)/s for 2 <= s <= 4.  [JS]: F decreases, f increases.
citations.hypotheses: formula domains as stated; the F formula is extended to [3, 5] from the delay equation (sF)' = f(s-1) (the note, section 0.1)

citations.statement: For x >= 285: V(x) = U_N/log x [1 + 1.45 th1 log N/(x-1) (1 + 10 log log N/log N)] (1 + 1.002 th2/(x-3)) (1 + th3/(2 log^2 x)), |th_i| <= 1, V(x) = prod_{p<x, p nmid N} (1 - 1/(p-1)).
For all x >= 45, sum_{n<=x} mu^2(n) <= 0.65 x.

citations.source: Johnston, Starichkova, arXiv:2208.01229v3 (numbering of the v3 PDF)
citations.statement: p_G(X2) = 0.65 (c_pi(X2) + 1/(16 pi)); c_4G(X2) = p_G(X2) + 0.9/(sqrt(X2) log log X2); Theorem 5.9 at X2 = exp(exp(5.077)), M = 18, alpha = 0.285, B = 2.01 gives S(A,P(z)) > 1.48 U_N N/log^2 N.
